newsitem.title: USA: Kantor says U.S. on right track with trade.
newsitem.headline: Kantor says U.S. on right track with trade.

text.p: The United States is moving in the right direction with regard to trade despite a smaller-than-expected decline in the August trade gap, U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor said Saturday.
Kantor stressed the strong increases in exports in recent years and played down the deficit.

"When you're growing faster than your trading partners, your (trade) deficit usually goes up," Kantor told reporters after meeting with the Business Council, a group of business leaders from very large U.S. corporations.
"We have a much stronger economy than any of our partners," he said. "So we're moving in the right direction."
The Commerce Department on Friday reported that the U.S. international trade deficit fell 6.6 percent to $10.83 billion in August from $11.6 billion in July.
Still, the overall level of the August trade gap was well above Wall Street economists' forecasts for $8.5 billion.

Asked about the status of discussions regarding China's entry into the World Trade Organization, Kantor replied, "We want China to become a member of the WTO but only on a commercially reasonable basis."
He also said that after a period of "intense strain" in the relationship with the Chinese over the issue, they have indicated a greater willingness to be flexible and pragmatic.

Asked whether the dollar/yen exchange rate was discussed in the meeting with business leaders, Kantor said it was not and he declined to comment on the currencies, deferring to U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, who generally speaks on the subject for the administration.
Kantor said he was asked by business leaders about his position on a proposal to combine the U.S. Trade Representative's office with the Commerce Department.

Kantor, who served as the U.S. Trade Representative before heading up the Commerce Department, said there was an inherent conflict of interest in the two jobs and that the departments should not be combined.
